BiblicalUsage: Ga'ar is a sharp rebuke, a word that stops something in its tracks. Jacob rebuked Joseph for his dream in Genesis 37:10, asking whether his whole family would bow down to him. God rebukes the rushing nations in Isaiah 17:13 until they flee like chaff before the wind, and the LORD rebukes the seed of corrupt priests in Malachi 2:3. Jeremiah is even asked why no one has reproved the false prophet in Jeremiah 29:27.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a rebuke from God is mercy wearing a hard face. It stops the nations, it stops the proud, and it stopped Joseph's family from missing what God was doing. I would rather be rebuked by God now than left alone in my error.
